title: EPF Withdrawal Rules: Form 121 Replaces Forms 15G and 15H
description: From April 1, 2026, a new declaration, Form 121, will replace Forms 15G and 15H for reducing TDS on certain incomes. This change impacts eligible taxpayers se.

faq.a: Form 121 is a new declaration form that will replace Forms 15G and 15H from April 1, 2026. It allows eligible taxpayers to declare that their total income for the financial year is below the basic exemption limit, requesting the payer not to deduct TDS on specified incomes.

While specific eligibility criteria will be detailed by the CBDT, it is expected to be available to resident individuals (both below and above 60 years of age) and HUFs whose estimated total income for the financial year results in a nil tax liability.

faq.q: When does Form 121 come into effect?
faq.a: Form 121 will replace Forms 15G and 15H starting from April 1, 2026, for the financial year 2026-27 and onwards.

faq.q: Does Form 121 make my EPF withdrawal tax-free?
faq.a: No, Form 121 is a declaration to avoid TDS deduction at source, not an exemption from tax. If your EPF withdrawal is taxable as per income tax laws, you are still liable to pay the applicable tax when filing your Income Tax Return.

faq.q: What happens if I don't submit Form 121 for an eligible EPF withdrawal?
faq.a: If you are eligible but do not submit Form 121 (or the equivalent form at that time), the EPFO will deduct TDS as per the applicable rates on your taxable EPF withdrawal. You can then claim credit for this TDS when you file your income tax return.
Similar to Forms 15G and 15H, Form 121 is expected to be valid for one financial year. You would need to submit a new form for each financial year if you continue to meet the eligibility conditions.

fact_check.summary: The article provides largely accurate information regarding the introduction of Form 121 and its implications for EPF withdrawals, aligning with current understanding and official timelines. However, there's a minor discrepancy in the stated TDS rate without PAN.
